prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t truthfully name a single “best” lawyer for every truck accident — the right attorney depends on your case facts, the lawyer’s truck-specific experience, resources, and how well you work together. I can, however, help you find a strong Dallas lawyer and tell you what to look for.

How to pick the best Dallas truck-accident lawyer
- Trucking experience: look for lawyers who routinely handle 18-wheeler/commercial-truck cases (not just general car-accident work).
- Regulatory knowledge: they should understand FMCSA rules, hours-of-service logs, DOT compliance, cargo and maintenance records.
- Resources and experts: the firm must retain accident reconstructionists, biomechanical experts, and investigators — truck cases often require expensive discovery.
- Trial experience: many large insurers only take claims seriously if the lawyer will try the case.
- Track record: past settlements/verdicts in truck cases (not just generic “personal injury” numbers).
- Reputation & reviews: peer recognition (Super Lawyers, Texas Trial Lawyers Association), client reviews, and Martindale-Hubbell ratings help.
- Board certification: Texas Board of Legal Specialization certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a plus.
- Communication & fee structure: contingency fee terms, how costs are advanced, and how the lawyer will keep you updated.

Important practical items
- Statute of limitations in Texas: generally 2 years from the date of injury for most personal-injury suits — act quickly.
- Preserve evidence: keep vehicle damage photos, medical records, phone/video, witness contacts, and don’t post details about the crash on social media.
- Don’t give recorded statements to insurers without your attorney.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many verdicts/settlements and typical range?
- Have you litigated against large trucking companies and their insurers?
- Do you have accident reconstruction and medical experts you use?
- Will you personally handle my case or pass it to an associate?
- What is your contingency fee and who pays litigation costs up front?
- Any disciplinary history or malpractice claims?
- Can you provide references from recent truck-accident clients?

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar website (attorney record/disciplines)
- Super Lawyers, Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google reviews
- Local trial-lawyer organizations and peer awards (Texas Trial Lawyers Association, Dallas Bar)

If you want, I can:
- Find and shortlist 3–5 Dallas lawyers/firms that specialize in truck cases (I’ll need your ZIP or neighborhood and a few case facts), or
- Draft a list of questions or an email you can use to contact firms.

Which would you prefer? If you want a shortlist, tell me your ZIP code and a brief description of the crash (date, injuries, owner/operator if known).
